title: Biosensor-based High Throughput Biopanning and Bioinformatics Analysis Strategy for the Global Validation of Drug-protein Interactions
protocol: Attach a ceramic sensor chip on the oscillator of a 27-MHz QCM apparatus.
Record the intrinsic frequency in the air phase before small molecule immobilization.
Detach the chip and pipette 20 μL of a solution (1 mM in 70% ethanol) of a small molecule derivative that forms SAM onto the gold electrode of the sensor chip.
Leave for 1 h at room temperature (around 20 °C) in a Petri dish with moistened tissue and shielded from room lights.
Wash the electrode surface gently with ultrapure water.
Remove the water drops by blowing air with a syringe or air duster.
Set up the sensor chip for the QCM apparatus.
Record the reduction in frequency in the air phase to measure the amount of the small molecule that has been immobilized.
Set a cuvette with a dedicated magnetic stirrer on the QCM biosensor and pour 8 mL of the reaction buffer into the cuvette.
Attach the QCM sensor chip to the oscillator.
Pull down the arm of the oscillator to immerse the chip into the buffer being stirred at 1000 rpm.
Start monitoring the QCM frequency on the personal computer (PC).
Wait until the sensorgram equilibrates to around 3 Hz/min of the frequency drift.
Inject 8 μL of a T7 phage library (1—2 × 10^10 pfu/mL) into the cuvette (final concentration: 1—2 × 10^7 pfu/mL).
Monitor the frequency reduction caused by the binding of T7 phages to the small molecule immobilized on the gold electrode surface for 10 min.
Stop the QCM frequency monitor.
Dislodge the sensor chip from the oscillator and remove the buffer by blowing air and/or wicking away with wipes.
Put the sensor chip into a humid Petri dish.
Drop 20 μL of the suspension of E. coli (BLT5615) host cells in the log phase onto the gold electrode.
Close the lid of the dish and cover it with aluminum foil to block out light.
Incubate the dish at 37 °C for 30 min on a 96-well microplate mixer at 1000-1500 rpm.
Recover 20 μL of the solution and suspend it into 200 μL of LB medium.
Prepare a dilution series of the phage solution for plaque isolation and DNA sequencing according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Wipe the gold electrode surface with a cotton swab soaked in 1% sodium dodecyl sulfate solution.
Wash the gold surface with ultrapure water from the washing bottle.
Dry the gold surface by blowing air or using wipes.
Drop 5 μL of piranha solution (Conc. H2SO4: 30% H2O2 = 3:1) on the gold surface and leave for 5 min.
Wash the gold surface again with water.
Dry the gold surface by blowing air and/or using wipes.
Drop 5 μL of piranha solution (Conc. H2SO4: 30% H2O2 = 3:1) on the gold surface and leave for 5 min.
Wash the gold surface again with water.
Dry the gold surface by blowing air and/or using wipes.
Unzip the stand-alone RELIC program suite on a PC with an MS Windows operating system.
Align the amino acid sequences of the 15-mer peptides affinity-selected using the drug or randomly selected from unscreened parent library in each text format file (name.txt).
Type the amino acid sequence of single or multiple protein(s) in each text file with FASTA format.
Download the database text files in FASTA format from any protein database.
Place the text files in the folder necessary for running each RELIC program.
Click the executable file (program.exe) for AADIV, INFO, MOTIF, MATCH, HETEROalign, FASTAcon, and FASTAskan to open Personal Version of FTN95.
Type the appropriate filename, along with the extension (name.txt), in the command message to execute each program.
Export the resulting text file to a spreadsheet software to generate a plot of information content or cumulative similarity scores.
